span.label: A DOSE-RESPONSE ON PRIME DURATION, MEASURED ON BEHAVIOUR: `the MAGNITUDE of the behavioral effects simply MIRRORED THE MAGNITUDE OF THE PERCEPTUAL INPUT. In Experiments 2 and 3, participants who were primed for 9 MIN showed stronger behavioral effects than participants who were primed for 2 MIN.` **Nine minutes against two, read off general-knowledge performance.** srull-wyer1979 doses by FREQUENCY of activation and measures a judgement; this doses by DURATION and measures what someone does - and the two papers are 19 years and one dependent-variable class apart
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE INFERENCE DRAWN FROM THE DOSE IS THE STEP WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY: `These results underscore the fact that the process under consideration can be characterized as rather PASSIVE.` **Dose-dependence is taken as evidence of passivity** - if the effect size simply tracks the amount of input, then no decision, strategy or correction is intervening to modulate it. That is a real argument and not an obvious one, and it is a different kind of claim from the measurement it rests on: the dose-response was measured, the passivity is inferred from its linearity
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A CONCEPTUAL REPLICATION WITH EVERYTHING CHANGED AT ONCE: `Quotation withheld.` **Three things varied simultaneously.** That buys generality and spends diagnosticity - a FAILURE would not have said which of the three was responsible, and a success cannot say which mattered. In a corpus that holds several papers on when priming effects replicate, the shape of a replication is worth recording as plainly as its outcome
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE PAPER PLACES ITSELF IN THE ACCESSIBILITY LINEAGE EXPLICITLY: `Quotation withheld.` **Both of those are in this corpus** - higgins1977 and srull-wyer1979, tagged earlier tonight. The claimed step is from judgement to BEHAVIOUR while keeping the same mechanism, so the 1977-79 accessibility work is not merely cited but load-bearing: if accessibility does not drive judgement, this paper has no base to extend from
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: stereotype —causes→ behavior
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE PAPER'S CENTRAL CLAIM, and `CORRESPONDING WITH SPECIFIC ATTRIBUTES` is the part that matters and is in the quote: the effect is not general arousal or mood but takes the CONTENT of the stereotype - professors improve general knowledge, hooligans reduce it. Weight 0.9: this is the discussion's opening summary of four experiments.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: perception —causes→ behavior
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.85 — **`THE AUTHORS EXPLAIN THEIR RESULTS BY CLAIMING` IS THE HEDGE AND IT IS THE FIRST CLAUSE OF THE QUOTE.** This is the paper's interpretation of its own four experiments, not a measured quantity - the measured thing is the duration dose-response (first sense), and `direct and pervasive` is what the authors conclude from it. Weight 0.85 for that gap.
